The Report Engine follows a strict separation:

```text
Analysis Engine
       =
DISCOVERS

Architecture Model
       =
DEFINES TRUTH

Evidence
       =
SUPPORTS TRUTH

Diagram Engine
       =
VISUALIZES

AI
       =
EXPLAINS

Report Engine
       =
ORGANIZES

Renderer
       =
PRESENTS
```

Therefore:

> **A StackSense report is a reproducible, versioned presentation of established architectural knowledge—not a second analysis system.**

The Report Engine should make the platform's results understandable to different audiences while preserving the exact relationship between:

```text
Finding
   ↓
Architecture
   ↓
Evidence
   ↓
Source
```

That provenance is more important than visual polish.

**End of Section 17.**



# 18. BACKEND ARCHITECTURE & MODULE BOUNDARIES

## 18.1 Purpose

This section defines the backend architecture of StackSense and establishes strict boundaries between backend modules.

The backend must be:

* modular;
* maintainable;
* testable;
* dependency-inverted;
* independently evolvable;
* suitable for production deployment;
* suitable for system-design evaluation;
* resistant to circular dependencies;
* explicit about ownership of business responsibilities.

The central principle is:

> **Each backend module owns a clearly defined business capability and exposes stable contracts to other modules. No module should reach into another module's internal implementation.**

---

# 18.2 Backend Architectural Style

StackSense will use a **modular layered architecture** with domain-oriented module boundaries.

Conceptually:

```text
                         API / HTTP
                             │
                             ▼
                    Application Services
                             │
                             ▼
                         Domain
                             │
                             ▼
                    Infrastructure
```

But this layering exists **inside modules** as well as across the backend.

The overall backend is:

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Presentation / API                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                  Application Services                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    Domain Modules                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Infrastructure / Adapters                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

# 18.3 Backend Is Not One Giant Application Module

The backend must not become:

```text
backend/
    services.py
    utils.py
    models.py
    everything.py
```

Instead, capabilities are explicitly separated.

The backend should conceptually contain modules such as:

```text
Platform
Identity
Organization
Repository
Analysis
Architecture
Knowledge
Diagram
Report
AI
Jobs
Notifications
```

The exact final package structure may evolve, but the ownership boundaries must remain.

---

# 18.4 High-Level Backend Architecture

```text
                         ┌───────────────┐
                         │    Client     │
                         └───────┬───────┘
                                 │
                                 ▼
                         ┌───────────────┐
                         │ API Layer     │
                         └───────┬───────┘
                                 │
        ┌────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┐
        │                        │                        │
        ▼                        ▼                        ▼
   Identity / Org          Repository / Analysis     Knowledge
        │                        │                        │
        │                        ▼                        │
        │                 Architecture Model             │
        │                        │                        │
        │             ┌──────────┼──────────┐             │
        │             ▼          ▼          ▼             │
        │           Graph      Search     Diagram        │
        │             │          │          │             │
        │             └──────────┼──────────┘             │
        │                        ▼                        │
        │                       RAG                       │
        │                        │                        │
        │                        ▼                        │
        │                       AI                        │
        │                                                 │
        └───────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
                     Background Jobs
                            │
                ┌───────────┼───────────┐
                ▼           ▼           ▼
             Queue       Workers     Scheduler
```

---

# 18.5 Core Backend Modules

The backend should be organized around the following major capabilities:

```text
1. Platform
2. Identity & Access
3. Organizations & Projects
4. Repository Management
5. Analysis
6. Architecture
7. Knowledge
8. Diagram
9. Report
10. AI
11. Jobs & Execution
12. Notifications
```

Not every module must have identical internal structure.

The important requirement is clear ownership.

---

# 18.6 Platform Module

The Platform module owns cross-cutting backend infrastructure that is not business-specific.

Responsibilities include:

* application bootstrap;
* configuration;
* dependency injection;
* lifecycle management;
* common error handling;
* health checks;
* logging setup;
* middleware;
* shared infrastructure contracts.

It must not contain business logic simply because the logic is "used everywhere."

---

# 18.7 Platform Must Remain Small

The Platform module is especially vulnerable to becoming a dumping ground.

Incorrect:

```text
platform/
    helpers.py
    business_logic.py
    random_service.py
```

The Platform module should contain only genuinely cross-cutting concerns.

---

# 18.8 Identity & Access Module

The Identity module owns:

* users;
* authentication;
* sessions/tokens;
* password-based authentication;
* JWT;
* OAuth/OIDC integration later;
* authorization primitives;
* roles/permissions.

The initially frozen direction is:

```text
Basic JWT Authentication
        ↓
Later OAuth/OIDC
```

OAuth must not force the initial architecture to depend on an external identity provider.

---

# 18.9 Authentication Boundary

Authentication answers:

> Who is this user?

Authorization answers:

> What is this user allowed to do?

These must remain separate concepts.

```text
Authentication
     ↓
Identity
     ↓
Authorization
     ↓
Resource Access
```

---

# 18.10 Organization & Project Module

This module owns the product hierarchy.

The core structure is:

```text
Organization
    ↓
Project
    ↓
Repository / Analysis / Architecture
```

Organizations are **not required to be globally unique by name**.

For example:

```text
Organization A
name = "Big MNC"

Organization B
name = "Big MNC"
```

may both exist.

The unique identity is the organization's internal ID/identifier, not its display name.

---

# 18.11 Organization Naming

Organization names are presentation/business data.

They must not be used as globally unique identifiers.

Preferred:

```text
organization_id = UUID
name = "Big MNC"
```

rather than:

```text
organization_name = globally unique key
```

---

# 18.12 Project Boundary

A Project belongs to an Organization.

A project owns or references:

* repositories;
* analysis runs;
* architecture versions;
* knowledge;
* diagrams;
* reports.

Project isolation is therefore a major authorization boundary.

---

# 18.13 Repository Management Module

Repository Management owns repository ingestion.

Responsibilities include:

* repository registration;
* repository source configuration;
* snapshot creation;
* branch/reference selection;
* commit metadata;
* repository artifact lifecycle;
* ingestion status.

It does not perform architectural interpretation.

---

# 18.14 Repository Module Boundary

Repository Management answers:

> What source should be analyzed?

Analysis answers:

> What does the source contain?

This distinction is mandatory.

---

# 18.15 Analysis Module

The Analysis module owns deterministic repository analysis.

Responsibilities include:

* file discovery;
* parsing;
* language detection;
* framework detection;
* symbol extraction;
* dependency extraction;
* API detection;
* configuration analysis;
* integration detection;
* finding generation.

The Analysis Engine is the authoritative owner of deterministic analysis.

---

# 18.16 Analysis Must Not Depend on AI

The primary analysis pipeline must work without an AI provider.

Correct:

```text
Repository
    ↓
Analysis
    ↓
Architecture
```

Optional:

```text
Architecture
    ↓
AI Explanation
```

Incorrect:

```text
Repository
    ↓
AI
    ↓
Analysis
```

---

# 18.17 Architecture Module

The Architecture module owns the canonical Architecture Model.

This is one of the most important backend boundaries.

Responsibilities include:

* architecture entities;
* architecture relationships;
* identity references;
* architecture versions;
* publication;
* validation;
* architecture queries.

---

# 18.18 Architecture as Canonical State

The Architecture module represents the answer to:

> What architecture has StackSense established for this repository snapshot?

Other systems may project or visualize this information.

They must not redefine it.

---

# 18.19 Architecture Module Does Not Own Analysis

Analysis discovers information.

Architecture organizes validated analysis results into canonical architectural state.

Therefore:

```text
Analysis
    ↓
Architecture
```

not:

```text
Architecture
    ↓
Analysis
```

---

# 18.20 Knowledge Module

The Knowledge module owns retrieval-oriented capabilities.

Responsibilities include:

* graph projection coordination;
* search projection coordination;
* retrieval;
* evidence planning;
* context construction;
* RAG orchestration.

It consumes the Architecture Model.

It does not become an alternative architecture source.

---

# 18.21 Knowledge Module Does Not Own AI

Knowledge may request an AI explanation, but AI provider infrastructure belongs to the AI module.

Preferred:

```text
Knowledge
    ↓
AI Application Contract
    ↓
AI Module
```

rather than:

```text
Knowledge
    ↓
Gemini SDK
```

---

# 18.22 Diagram Module

The Diagram module owns visual architecture generation.

Responsibilities include:

* view definitions;
* entity/relationship filtering;
* Diagram Specifications;
* layout coordination;
* ELK integration;
* diagram caching;
* diagram export coordination.

It consumes Architecture Model data.

---

# 18.23 Diagram Module Does Not Discover Architecture

The Diagram module must never parse source files to determine:

> What nodes should exist?

That belongs to Analysis/Architecture.

Diagram generation starts from established architecture.

---

# 18.24 Report Module

The Report module owns:

* report templates;
* report specifications;
* report section generation;
* renderers;
* artifact creation;
* report lifecycle;
* report metadata.

It consumes established analysis/architecture data.

---

# 18.25 Report Module Does Not Recalculate Findings

For example, if Analysis says:

```text
severity = HIGH
```

Report must render:

```text
HIGH
```

It must not independently decide:

```text
severity = CRITICAL
```

---

# 18.26 AI Module

The AI module owns:

* AI provider abstraction;
* provider factory;
* provider adapters;
* AI request normalization;
* response normalization;
* provider health;
* provider fallback;
* AI-specific policies.

It does not own:

* architecture;
* repository analysis;
* graph truth;
* search truth.

---

# 18.27 Jobs & Execution Module

The Jobs module owns asynchronous execution.

Responsibilities include:

* job creation;
* queue integration;
* workers;
* job state;
* retry policies;
* idempotency;
* execution metadata;
* cancellation;
* scheduling integration.

The queue infrastructure is an execution mechanism, not a domain owner.

---

# 18.28 Queue Boundary

The queue must not contain business rules.

Correct:

```text
Analysis Service
    ↓
Create Analysis Job
    ↓
Queue
    ↓
Analysis Worker
    ↓
Analysis Service
```

Incorrect:

```text
Queue
    ↓
contains analysis business logic
```

---

# 18.29 Notifications Module

Notifications own:

* notification events;
* delivery;
* SSE events;
* future email/webhook integrations;
* notification preferences.

Notifications should not contain the business logic that caused the event.

Example:

```text
Analysis Completed
        ↓
Domain Event
        ↓
Notification
        ↓
SSE
```

---

# 18.30 Backend Layering

Within a module, the preferred layering is:

```text
module/
├── api/
├── application/
├── domain/
└── infrastructure/
```

Conceptually:

```text
API
 ↓
Application
 ↓
Domain
 ↑
Infrastructure adapters
```

The exact folder names may vary, but the dependency direction must be preserved.

---

# 18.31 API Layer

The API layer owns:

* HTTP routes;
* request parsing;
* response serialization;
* authentication extraction;
* API-level validation;
* HTTP error mapping.

It should remain thin.

---

# 18.32 API Layer Must Not Contain Business Logic

Incorrect:

```text
POST /analysis

route:
    parse repository
    analyze files
    create architecture
    generate graph
    call AI
```

Preferred:

```text
POST /analysis
      ↓
AnalysisApplicationService
      ↓
Domain / Infrastructure
```

---

# 18.33 Application Layer

The Application layer coordinates use cases.

Examples:

```text
CreateProject
StartAnalysis
PublishArchitecture
GenerateDiagram
GenerateReport
AskArchitectureQuestion
```

Application services orchestrate domain operations and infrastructure ports.

---

# 18.34 Application Services Are Use-Case Oriented

Avoid generic services such as:

```text
EverythingService
CommonService
DataService
```

Prefer explicit use cases.

For example:

```text
StartAnalysisService
PublishArchitectureService
GenerateReportService
AskKnowledgeQuestionService
```

---

# 18.35 Domain Layer

The Domain layer owns business rules.

Examples:

* architecture version state;
* project ownership rules;
* analysis lifecycle;
* report lifecycle;
* authorization policies;
* job state transitions.

Domain logic should not depend on:

* FastAPI;
* Django;
* Express;
* SQLAlchemy;
* Elasticsearch SDK;
* Neo4j SDK;
* Gemini SDK.

---

# 18.36 Infrastructure Layer

Infrastructure implements external dependencies.

Examples:

```text
PostgreSQL
Redis
Neo4j
Elasticsearch
Filesystem
S3
AI Providers
Queue
Git Providers
```

Infrastructure adapters implement interfaces defined by the application/domain boundary where appropriate.

---

# 18.37 Dependency Direction

The preferred dependency direction is:

```text
API
 ↓
Application
 ↓
Domain

Infrastructure
 ─────implements────→ Application/Domain ports
```

The domain must not depend on infrastructure.

---

# 18.38 Dependency Inversion

For example:

```text
ArchitectureApplicationService
          ↓
ArchitectureRepository
          ↑
PostgresArchitectureRepository
```

The application depends on the abstraction.

The PostgreSQL implementation depends on that abstraction.

---

# 18.39 External Services as Adapters

External systems should be behind adapters.

Examples:

```text
GitRepository
    ↑
GitHubRepositoryAdapter

AIProvider
    ↑
GeminiProvider

ArtifactStorage
    ↑
LocalArtifactStorage

ArtifactStorage
    ↑
S3ArtifactStorage
```

---

# 18.40 Module Public Interface

Each module should expose a limited public interface.

For example:

```text
architecture/
    public:
        ArchitectureQuery
        ArchitectureService
        ArchitectureRepository
```

Internal implementation details remain private.

---

# 18.41 No Deep Imports

Other modules should not import:

```text
architecture.infrastructure.neo4j.internal_repository
```

Instead:

```text
architecture.application
architecture.public_contract
```

should provide the required interface.

---

# 18.42 Cross-Module Communication

Modules may communicate through:

1. application service contracts;
2. domain events;
3. explicit query interfaces;
4. shared immutable value objects where justified.

They should not communicate by directly accessing another module's database tables or internal classes.

---

# 18.43 Direct Database Access Rule

A module must not directly query another module's tables.

Incorrect:

```text
Report
   ↓
SELECT * FROM analysis_internal_tables
```

Preferred:

```text
Report
   ↓
Analysis Query Contract
   ↓
Analysis Module
```

This protects module ownership.

---

# 18.44 Shared Database

The backend may initially use one PostgreSQL deployment.

That does **not** mean all modules have unrestricted access to all tables.

Logical ownership remains:

```text
Analysis owns analysis tables
Architecture owns architecture tables
Reports own report tables
```

---

# 18.45 Modular Monolith

The initial backend should be implemented as a **modular monolith**.

This means:

```text
One Deployment
      +
One Backend Application
      +
Strong Internal Module Boundaries
```

rather than immediately deploying every module as a microservice.

---

# 18.46 Why Modular Monolith

This provides:

* simpler deployment;
* simpler local development;
* lower infrastructure overhead;
* easier transactions;
* easier debugging;
* strong boundaries;
* future extraction potential.

It is appropriate for StackSense's current scale.

---

# 18.47 Future Service Extraction

If a module later needs independent scaling, it should be possible to extract it.

For example:

```text
Current:
Backend
 ├── Analysis
 ├── Knowledge
 └── Reports
```

Future:

```text
Analysis Service
Knowledge Service
Report Service
```

The internal contracts should make this transition manageable.

---

# 18.48 Do Not Prematurely Build Microservices

StackSense must not introduce microservices solely for architectural aesthetics.

The system-design value comes from:

* clear boundaries;
* explicit contracts;
* asynchronous processing;
* dependency inversion;
* scalable execution.

A modular monolith demonstrates these principles without unnecessary operational complexity.

---

# 18.49 Module Dependency Graph

The conceptual dependency graph is:

```text
                    Platform
                       ↑
                       │
              Identity / Access
                       │
                Organizations
                       │
                    Project
                       │
                  Repository
                       │
                    Analysis
                       │
                  Architecture
                  /    |     \
                 /     |      \
                ↓      ↓       ↓
           Knowledge Diagram  Report
              │        │        │
              │        │        │
              └────────┼────────┘
                       ↓
                      AI
```

This is conceptual; modules should not create unnecessary bidirectional dependencies.

---

# 18.50 More Precise Dependency Direction

A cleaner representation is:

```text
Platform
   ↑
Identity / Organization
   ↑
Repository
   ↑
Analysis
   ↓
Architecture
   ↓
┌───────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┐
↓               ↓               ↓
Knowledge      Diagram         Report
↓               ↓               ↓
AI            Layout          Storage
```

The arrows represent dependency/consumption relationships, not necessarily runtime call direction.

---

# 18.51 Architecture as Shared Boundary

Many modules consume Architecture Model information.

Therefore the Architecture module should expose stable query contracts.

For example:

```text
ArchitectureQuery
    get_entity()
    get_entities()
    get_relationships()
    get_version()
```

Consumers do not need to know how architecture is stored.

---

# 18.52 Analysis to Architecture Contract

Analysis produces validated analysis output.

Architecture consumes:

```text
Analysis Result
```

and produces:

```text
Architecture Version
```

The transformation must be deterministic.

---

# 18.53 Architecture to Knowledge Contract

Knowledge consumes:

```text
Architecture Model
```

and produces projections/retrieval contexts.

It must not modify canonical architecture during retrieval.

---

# 18.54 Architecture to Diagram Contract

Diagram consumes:

```text
Architecture Query
```

and produces:

```text
Diagram Specification
```

---

# 18.55 Architecture to Report Contract

Report consumes:

```text
Architecture
+
Findings
+
Evidence
```

and produces:

```text
Report Specification
```

---

# 18.56 Knowledge to AI Contract

Knowledge produces:

```text
Knowledge Context
```

AI consumes:

```text
AI Request
```

and produces:

```text
AI Response
```

This keeps retrieval and provider infrastructure separate.

---

# 18.57 Report to AI Contract

Report may optionally request:

```text
Executive Summary
```

from AI.

The request should contain a bounded Knowledge Context.

Report should not directly access provider SDKs.

---

# 18.58 Diagram to Knowledge Contract

Diagram may provide navigation into Knowledge.

For example:

```text
Node selected
    ↓
Architecture Entity ID
    ↓
Knowledge Query
```

The Diagram module does not directly query Elasticsearch.

---

# 18.59 Events

Cross-module asynchronous events should be used where loose coupling is useful.

Examples:

```text
RepositorySnapshotCreated
AnalysisCompleted
ArchitecturePublished
ReportGenerated
ProjectionCompleted
```

---

# 18.60 Domain Events

A domain event represents a meaningful state transition.

Example:

```text
ArchitecturePublished
```

may trigger:

```text
Graph Projection
Search Projection
Diagram Cache Invalidation
Notification
```

without Architecture directly calling every consumer.

---

# 18.61 Event Consumers

Example:

```text
ArchitecturePublished
       │
       ├── Knowledge Projection Worker
       ├── Diagram Cache Handler
       ├── Notification Handler
       └── Report Availability Handler
```

This reduces coupling.

---

# 18.62 Event Ownership

The module that owns the business state owns the event.

For example:

```text
ArchitecturePublished
```

belongs to Architecture.

Knowledge consumes it.

Knowledge does not redefine it.

---

# 18.63 Event Payload

Events should contain stable identifiers rather than huge payloads.

Example:

```text
ArchitecturePublished
├── event_id
├── project_id
├── architecture_version_id
├── published_at
```

Consumers can retrieve required details through contracts.

---

# 18.64 Event Reliability

Important events should support:

* idempotent consumers;
* retries;
* durable delivery where required;
* observability;
* dead-letter handling.

The event system must not silently lose critical state transitions.

---

# 18.65 Synchronous vs Asynchronous

Use synchronous communication when:

* the user needs an immediate result;
* the operation is small;
* consistency is required immediately.

Use asynchronous jobs/events when:

* analysis is long-running;
* report generation is large;
* projection is expensive;
* AI generation is slow;
* diagram generation is large.

---

# 18.66 Example: Analysis

User starts analysis:

```text
POST /analysis
       ↓
AnalysisApplicationService
       ↓
Create Analysis Job
       ↓
Queue
       ↓
Worker
       ↓
Analysis Engine
       ↓
Architecture
       ↓
ArchitecturePublished
```

The API does not wait for the entire repository analysis.

---

# 18.67 Example: Knowledge Projection

```text
ArchitecturePublished
       ↓
Projection Job
       ├── Neo4j Projection
       └── Elasticsearch Projection
```

Failures are independently retryable.

---

# 18.68 Example: Report

```text
POST /reports
       ↓
ReportApplicationService
       ↓
Report Job
       ↓
Queue
       ↓
Worker
       ↓
Report Engine
       ↓
Artifact Storage
```

---

# 18.69 Example: AI Question

For an interactive question:

```text
POST /knowledge/query
       ↓
Knowledge Service
       ↓
Retrieve Evidence
       ↓
AI Provider
       ↓
Response
```

For long-running generation:

```text
Knowledge Query
       ↓
AI Job
       ↓
Worker
       ↓
AI Provider
       ↓
SSE
```

---

# 18.70 Shared Kernel

A small shared kernel may exist for genuinely universal concepts.

Potential examples:

```text
ProjectId
OrganizationId
ArchitectureVersionId
RepositoryId
JobId
```

Shared kernel must remain intentionally small.

---

# 18.71 Shared Kernel Must Not Become a Dumping Ground

Avoid:

```text
shared/
    all_models.py
    all_services.py
    utils.py
```

A shared module should contain only concepts that truly belong across boundaries.

---

# 18.72 Value Objects

Value objects may be shared where semantics are identical.

Examples:

```text
EntityId
ProjectId
ArchitectureVersion
SourceLocation
```

But duplication may sometimes be preferable to coupling.

The shared kernel should therefore remain conservative.

---

# 18.73 Common Utilities

Generic infrastructure utilities may be shared:

* time abstractions;
* UUID generation;
* pagination primitives;
* structured logging;
* error primitives.

Business-specific helpers should remain inside their owning modules.

---

# 18.74 Error Ownership

Each module owns its domain errors.

Example:

```text
ArchitectureVersionNotFound
```

belongs to Architecture.

```text
AnalysisNotFound
```

belongs to Analysis.

The API layer maps domain/application errors into HTTP responses.

---

# 18.75 Error Translation

Example:

```text
Domain Error
    ↓
Application Layer
    ↓
API Error Mapper
    ↓
HTTP 404 / 409 / 422 / 500
```

Infrastructure exceptions should not leak directly to clients.

---

# 18.76 Transaction Boundaries

Transactions should be owned by application use cases.

Example:

```text
PublishArchitecture
       ↓
Transaction
       ├── persist architecture
       └── record publication state
```

External systems such as Neo4j or Elasticsearch should not normally participate in the same PostgreSQL transaction.

Their consistency is handled asynchronously.

---

# 18.77 Eventual Consistency

The architecture explicitly accepts eventual consistency for derived projections.

Example:

```text
Architecture V15
       ↓
Published immediately

Neo4j V15
       ↓
May become ready shortly afterward

Elasticsearch V15
       ↓
May become ready shortly afterward
```

The system tracks projection state.

---

# 18.78 Canonical vs Derived State

Canonical:

```text
Architecture Model
Analysis Results
Identity
Project State
```

Derived:

```text
Neo4j
Elasticsearch
Diagrams
Reports
AI summaries
Caches
```

This distinction must remain consistent throughout the backend.

---

# 18.79 Module Data Ownership

Conceptually:

| Module        | Owns                                           |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Identity      | Users, authentication, permissions             |
| Organization  | Organizations, projects                        |
| Repository    | Repository registrations and snapshots         |
| Analysis      | Analysis runs and deterministic findings       |
| Architecture  | Architecture entities, relationships, versions |
| Knowledge     | Retrieval/projection state                     |
| Diagram       | Diagram definitions/cache/layout state         |
| Report        | Reports/templates/artifacts                    |
| AI            | Provider configuration/runtime metadata        |
| Jobs          | Job lifecycle/execution                        |
| Notifications | Notification state/delivery                    |

---

# 18.80 Database Ownership

Each module should own its persistence model.

Example:

```text
Identity
    users
    sessions

Organization
    organizations
    projects

Analysis
    analysis_runs
    findings

Architecture
    architecture_versions
    entities
    relationships

Report
    reports
    report_artifacts
```

The exact schema may vary.

The ownership principle does not.

---

# 18.81 Repository Pattern

Repositories should belong to the module whose aggregate/data they manage.

For example:

```text
architecture/
    domain/
    application/
    infrastructure/
        postgres_architecture_repository.py
```

rather than:

```text
shared/
    repositories.py
```

containing everything.

---

# 18.82 No Generic Repository Abstraction Everywhere

Avoid creating abstractions solely for architectural decoration.

For example:

```text
GenericRepository[T]
```

should not automatically be used for every domain.

Repositories should express meaningful persistence operations.

---

# 18.83 Service Ownership

A service should belong to the module that owns the use case.

Example:

```text
GenerateReportService
```

belongs to Report.

Not:

```text
shared/
    services.py
```

---

# 18.84 Circular Dependency Prevention

The architecture must prevent cycles such as:

```text
Analysis
   ↓
Report
   ↓
Analysis
```

or:

```text
Knowledge
   ↓
Architecture
   ↓
Knowledge
```

where both modules directly depend on each other's internals.

---

# 18.85 Breaking Cycles

If two modules need to react to one another, use:

* stable contracts;
* domain events;
* query interfaces;
* shared value objects.

For example:

```text
Architecture
     ↓
ArchitecturePublished
     ↓
Knowledge
```

instead of:

```text
Architecture ↔ Knowledge
```

---

# 18.86 Dependency Rule

A module may depend on another module's **public contract**, not its internals.

Allowed:

```text
Report
   ↓
ArchitectureQuery
```

Not allowed:

```text
Report
   ↓
Architecture.infrastructure.postgres.internal
```

---

# 18.87 Backend Framework Boundary

The backend framework must remain an infrastructure/presentation concern.

Whether the backend uses the selected Python framework, framework-specific controllers should not leak into domain logic.

Conceptually:

```text
Framework
    ↓
API Adapter
    ↓
Application
    ↓
Domain
```

This keeps core business logic framework-independent.

---

# 18.88 Async Worker Boundary

Workers should be thin execution adapters.

Incorrect:

```text
Worker
    ↓
contains all analysis business logic
```

Preferred:

```text
Worker
    ↓
Application Service
    ↓
Domain
```

The same application use case should ideally be callable from:

* HTTP;
* worker;
* scheduled task;
* CLI/test harness.

---

# 18.89 Scheduler Boundary

The Scheduler decides:

> When should this job run?

The Job/Application layer decides:

> What should the job do?

This separation is important.

```text
Scheduler
    ↓
Create/Trigger Job
    ↓
Application Service
```

---

# 18.90 Queue Boundary

The queue answers:

> How is asynchronous work transported?

It does not answer:

> What does this business operation mean?

This keeps infrastructure replaceable.

---

# 18.91 Redis Boundary

Redis may be used for:

* queue transport;
* caching;
* transient state;
* rate limiting where appropriate.

Redis must not become the canonical storage for Architecture Model data.

---

# 18.92 PostgreSQL Boundary

PostgreSQL is the primary transactional persistence layer.

It should own durable canonical application state.

Examples:

* users;
* organizations;
* projects;
* analysis metadata;
* Architecture Model;
* reports;
* jobs.

---

# 18.93 Neo4j Boundary

Neo4j owns graph projection data.

It is optimized for:

* traversal;
* relationships;
* impact analysis.

It is not the canonical Architecture Model store.

---

# 18.94 Elasticsearch Boundary

Elasticsearch owns search/retrieval projections.

It is optimized for:

* full-text search;
* semantic retrieval;
* filtering;
* ranking.

It is not the canonical source.

---

# 18.95 Filesystem/S3 Boundary

Artifact storage owns generated files.

Initially:

```text
LocalArtifactStorage
```

Future:

```text
S3ArtifactStorage
```

The Report module uses the abstraction.

---

# 18.96 AI Boundary

AI infrastructure owns provider communication.

No other module should directly use:

```text
Gemini SDK
Ollama API
OpenAI-compatible SDK
```

---

# 18.97 Cross-Cutting Concerns

The following should be handled consistently across modules:

* authentication;
* authorization;
* logging;
* metrics;
* tracing;
* error handling;
* configuration;
* rate limiting;
* audit logging;
* request IDs;
* correlation IDs.

These belong primarily to Platform/API infrastructure, while domain-specific authorization remains owned by the relevant module.

---

# 18.98 Authorization Boundary

Authorization must occur at the resource boundary.

Example:

```text
GET /projects/{project_id}/architecture
       ↓
Authentication
       ↓
Authorization
       ↓
Architecture Query
```

The Architecture module should not assume that the API layer has performed every domain-specific authorization check.

---

# 18.99 Defense in Depth

Security should exist at multiple layers.

```text
API
 ↓
Authorization
 ↓
Application Service
 ↓
Domain Policy
 ↓
Repository Scope
```

This reduces accidental cross-tenant access.

---

# 18.100 Module Observability

Every module should expose meaningful operational signals.

Examples:

```text
Analysis:
    analysis duration
    files processed
    failures

Architecture:
    versions published
    entity count
    relationship count

Knowledge:
    retrieval latency
    projection lag

Diagram:
    generation time
    graph size

Report:
    generation time
    rendering failures

AI:
    latency
    provider failures
    fallback count

Jobs:
    queue latency
    retry count
    failure rate
```

---

# 18.101 Module Health

Health checks should distinguish:

```text
Application Healthy
```

from:

```text
Optional Dependency Degraded
```

For example:

```text
PostgreSQL = HEALTHY
Neo4j = UNAVAILABLE
Elasticsearch = HEALTHY
AI = DEGRADED
```

The backend may still provide core functionality.

---

# 18.102 Backend Failure Isolation

Failure of one derived capability should not cascade unnecessarily.

Example:

```text
AI unavailable
    ↓
Reports still work deterministically
    ↓
Architecture still works
```

Similarly:

```text
Elasticsearch unavailable
    ↓
Architecture still works
    ↓
Graph queries may still work
```

---

# 18.103 API Version Boundary

External API contracts should use:

```text
/api/v1/
```

as previously frozen.

Internal module contracts may evolve independently as long as compatibility is maintained where required.

---

# 18.104 DTO Boundary

API DTOs should not automatically become domain models.

Preferred:

```text
HTTP Request DTO
       ↓
Application Command
       ↓
Domain
```

and:

```text
Domain Result
       ↓
Response DTO
       ↓
HTTP
```

This prevents API contracts from contaminating domain semantics.

---

# 18.105 Domain Model Boundary

Database ORM models should likewise not automatically become domain entities.

Preferred:

```text
ORM Model
    ↓
Repository Mapping
    ↓
Domain Entity
```

This allows persistence details to evolve independently.

---

# 18.106 Backend Directory Concept

A conceptual backend structure is:

```text
backend/
│
├── platform/
│   ├── config/

│   ├── middleware/

│   ├── domain/
│   └── infrastructure/

├── organizations/
│   ├── api/
│   ├── application/
│   ├── domain/
│   └── infrastructure/
│
├── repositories/
│   ├── api/
│   ├── application/
│   ├── domain/
│   └── infrastructure/
│
├── analysis/
│   ├── api/
│   ├── application/
│   ├── domain/
│   └── infrastructure/
│

│   ├── api/
│   ├── application/
│   ├── domain/
```
